the use of UF milk and pre-fermentation in the manufacture of Prato cheese, especially with 20% of the milk pre-fermented and the only one with indirect heating of the curd, resulted in cheese with a better sensory profile.
the cheese produced using UF milk, pre-fermented with 20% of the same milk, and heated in the vat, was the one with the best acceptance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the use of ultrafiltered milk and pre-fermentation of the curd, with or without indirect heat application, are viable alternatives for the production of Prato cheese.

the use of ultrafiltration and pre-fermentations of 20% of the same milk in the cheese manufacturing process, with indirect heating, was the most effective treatment for the production of Prato cheese.
the use of UF milk, pre-fermentation and indirect heating of the mass, in the manufacture of Prato cheese, was effective in improving the sensory characteristics of the product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of UF milk for making cheese can result in a product with a higher fat content, which is an important characteristic of cheese, as it is related to its sensory characteristics.
the use of a pre-fermented concentrate and the use of indirect heating during cooking are important to improve the sensory characteristics of the cheeses.
the process of cheese-making is a complex system that is affected by many different factors, and that the use of ultrafiltration in cheese-making is not a simple solution to all problems.
